name: Multiple Epiphyseal Dysplasia-Miniepiphyses Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Multiple Epiphyseal Dysplasia-Miniepiphyses Syndrome

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of multiple small and irregular epiphyses (miniepiphyses) affecting long bones
Clinical presence of joint stiffness and mild misalignment without severe deformity
Mild short stature or growth retardation apparent in childhood
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with epiphyseal dysplasia (e.g., COMP, MATN3)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic radiographic epiphyseal abnormalities plus clinical joint involvement; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on radiological findings combined with clinical features; genetic testing can aid but may not always detect causative mutations.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple small irregular epiphyses (miniepiphyses) on radiographs
searchTerms: many small irregular bone ends on X-ray

pathognomonic.symptomName: Joint stiffness predominantly affecting large joints
searchTerms: joint stiffness mainly in large joints

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mild short stature with disproportionate limb length
searchTerms: slightly short height with uneven limbs
mild short stature with limb disproportion
short height with limb length differences

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in knees and hips
searchTerms: reduced motion in hips and knees

common.symptomName: Gait abnormalities due to joint involvement
searchTerms: abnormal walking due to joint problems
joint wear and tear starting young

occasional.symptomName: Muscle weakness secondary to joint dysfunction
searchTerms: weak muscles due to joint dysfunction
reduced strength linked to joint issues

occasional.symptomName: Delayed bone age on radiographic assessment
searchTerms: bones appear younger than actual age on X-ray
slow bone development seen on imaging

rare.symptomName: Epiphyseal irregularities in small bones of hands and feet
searchTerms: irregular bone ends in hands and feet
hand and foot bone tip irregularities

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; absence of inflammatory markers
imaging: Radiographs showing multiple small, irregular epiphyses (miniepiphyses) in long bones
Possible early degenerative changes in affected joints
genetic: Pathogenic variants in COMP, MATN3, or other genes associated with epiphyseal dysplasia
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Larger epiphyses compared to miniepiphyses syndrome
Different genetic mutations (e.g., COMP mutations more common)
Involvement of spine with significant vertebral abnormalities

redFlags: Severe joint deformities causing functional impairment
Signs of inflammatory arthritis or systemic illness
